change: ContentViolationMediaTooLarge.byteSize was integer, and is integer (int64)
reason: A file's size in bytes passes what 32 bits hold (a video may be 1 GiB and more), so the document now says it is a 64-bit integer. Nothing changes on the wire: the JSON number is the same. The typed SDKs widen the field (Go int to int64, Java Integer to Long, .NET int to long, Rust i32 to i64): code that keeps the value in a 32-bit variable changes its type.

change: GET, PUT and DELETE /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/assistant/image-provider refuse an OAuth client other than Peal's command line (403 Forbidden, missingPermission assistant:configure), whatever its scopes
reason: Since the image provider endpoints shipped (2026-11-12), an application connected with workspace:write could point a workspace's image prompts, and now its drafts, at a server of its own, which kept receiving them after its grant was revoked. assistant:configure now reaches no OAuth client but Peal's command line; owners and admins in their own session, the command line, and API keys or partner keys given the permission keep it. An application that set a provider asks the person to set it in the web app, or uses an API key given assistant:configure.

change: The SDKs' BadGatewayErrorBody (one type for every 502 body with several errors) names TextProviderRefused and AssistantFailed, no longer AssistantFailed and ImageProviderRefused; AssistantFailedEncoded lost its _tag field, and its tag type (AssistantFailedEncodedTag, AssistantFailedEncoded.Tag) is gone
reason: The suggestions endpoint and the text provider's test now answer 502 with two errors each, and the generator names a single body type for each status, after one of the endpoints that has a union there. Nothing changes on the wire: every 502 body still carries its _tag. Code that matched BadGatewayErrorBody.ImageProviderRefused, or read AssistantFailedEncoded's _tag through its type, reads the body's _tag as a string instead. The SDKs are 0.x: this ships in their next minor release, 0.4.0, whose notes say so.

change: A post.cancelled webhook may name one channel taken off a post that still goes out on its others (scope: "target"), as well as a cancelled post (scope: "post")
reason: Removing one channel from a scheduled post (DELETE …/posts/{postId}/targets/{targetId}) is told as a post.cancelled naming that channel alone, as a channel cancelled while its post was going out already was. A receiver that marked the whole post cancelled on every post.cancelled reads the new scope field: "target" means the post still goes out on its other channels. Events made before the field was sent have none, and are about the post.

change: The SDKs' 402 error (PaymentRequiredError) no longer carries a typed PlanLimitReachedEncoded body on any endpoint: its body is untyped, and PaymentRequiredErrorBody (PlanLimitReachedEncoded or UsageAllowanceReachedEncoded) is the type to read it as; Rust's ApiError::PaymentRequiredError lost its fields (tag, code, request_id, allowed, billing_url, limit, plan, plan_with_room, used)
reason: Four endpoints (suggestions, images, an inbox reply, a boost) now answer 402 with two errors, PlanLimitReached and UsageAllowanceReached, and the generator names a single body type for each status, as for 502 before. Nothing changes on the wire: every 402 body still carries its _tag and the same fields, billingUrl included. Code that read PaymentRequiredError.body's fields through its type reads the body's _tag, then the fields, as PaymentRequiredErrorBody. The SDKs are 0.x: this ships in their next minor release, whose notes say so.

change: On a server that bills, POST …/assistant/suggestions and POST …/assistant/images answer 402 UsageAllowanceReached to a billing account without a payment method (paymentMethodRequired), where a daily quota answered before, and past the month's allowance or ceiling to one that pays
reason: The writing assistant on the server's models is a meter of the billing account (wave T, part T7): it needs a payment method, includes a monthly allowance, and bills past it up to a ceiling. A workspace's own text or image provider is not metered; a legacy plan keeps its daily quota; a server that does not bill is unchanged.

change: On a server that bills, POST …/inbox/comments/{commentId}/replies and POST …/ads/boosts may answer 402 UsageAllowanceReached once the billing account used the inbox messages or managed ads its month allows without a payment method, or on a legacy plan, or while its payment fails
reason: Outbound messages and managed ads are meters of the billing account (T7). Reading, publishing and running boosts are never metered; a reply sent again under its Idempotency-Key answers the reply it made.
